title: AI Agent Onboarding
riido_task: RIID-4720 [Contracts] AI Agent onboarding fixture projection
summary: AI Agent onboarding fixture behavior is generated from the client API DSL/IR/OpenAPI fixture set; policy prose is not a second authority.
invariants: client-local onboarding draft/configuration selection remains non-durable until workspace_id and runtime_id are known.
fixture-created agents are ordinary agents with non-unique names; the control plane must not auto-suffix display names.
Direct setting is client presentation, not an AgentOnboardingFixture.
Runtime/provider install rows are presentation over device/runtime liveness, not provider-install commands.
Only fixture creates use CreateOnboardingAgentRequest; its optional request_id is 1..128 ASCII bytes matching ^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,128}$. Direct configuration create keeps its existing seven fields.

The authorized principal, resolved workspace and fixture-create operation scope the key; identical full creation payload and fixture_id replay the same agent_id with HTTP 201 until 24 hours after the original server-recorded creation-attempt timestamp, including response loss or restart.

A changed payload or fixture_id, a deleted replay target, or the same agent_id reused with a different agent CreatedAt incarnation returns HTTP 409 without creating, recreating, or returning the replacement agent. v1/v2 aliases share the fixture-create scope; task completion receipts remain separate.

The private hashed receipt and agent creation commit together; fixture creation emits no create event and this contract adds none. Capacity exhaustion returns HTTP 503 before creation and never evicts unexpired receipts.

The guaranteed replay window ends 24 hours after the original server-recorded creation-attempt timestamp (receipt created_at), not after HTTP acknowledgement; after expiry a new create is possible. Callers without request_id retain independent-create behavior and have no duplicate-prevention guarantee.

loop.observation: A lost fixture-create response could cause an onboarding retry to create another ordinary agent because the original create request had no idempotency identity.
loop.hypothesis: A small verifier can make onboarding drift observable by deriving a reader and evidence from DSL, IR, OpenAPI, and product fixture-row anchors.
loop.execute: Verify the fixture-only request_id schema, separate direct-create shape, durable scoped replay/conflict/retention/capacity scenarios, fixture catalog, DSL/IR/OpenAPI and generated reader.
loop.evaluate: CI fails when onboarding operation tuples, schema fields, fixture row anchors, generated reader text, or no-diff route boundaries drift.
loop.retrospective: Future onboarding behavior should update this manifest and API fixture first, then regenerate the reader instead of editing long-form policy prose.
